conditions: x is any finite real number, including -1, 0, and 1; sqrt is the nonnegative real square root and ln is the real logarithm.
An explicit exact antiderivative differentiable on the entire real axis is required, up to one global additive constant.
The substitution is not globally monotone; its stationary points must not become domain exclusions or branch boundaries.
x is real with 0<x<1; sqrt is the positive real square root on this interval.
atan is the principal real inverse tangent. An explicit exact antiderivative is required throughout (0,1), up to one additive constant.
Endpoint limits may be stated, but neither endpoint is part of the required differentiation domain.
